analysis.one_liner: Torrent Pharmaceuticals makes branded generic medicines for India and export markets like Brazil and Germany, and since January 2026 has absorbed JB Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals, adding a US-generics and contract manufacturing business.
analysis.whats_happening: Torrent's board meets on 23 October 2026 (within the week) to approve Q2 FY27 results and host the analyst call. The last reported quarter, Q1 FY27 (June 2026), was the first full quarter after the JB Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals merger legally completed in July 2026, so revenue jumped 55% YoY but that figure blends Torrent's own growth with JB's entire business being added in - not an apples-to-apples comparison. Separately, the company's Bileshwarpura and Dahej plants both cleared recent USFDA inspections with zero observations, and an Executive Director, Amal Kelshikar, resigned effective 16 October 2026.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a well-run Indian pharma company that just got a lot bigger by merging with JB Chemicals, which brings US generics and contract manufacturing exposure Torrent didn't have before. The catch: because the merger folded in a new company's full revenue, you cannot simply compare this year's sales to last year's and call it organic growth - management says the pre-merger Torrent business itself grew around 17%, which is the more honest number. Profit (PAT) has grown much slower than revenue because the deal was debt-funded and carries integration and amortisation costs, so the next few quarters will show whether that gap closes.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026): revenue ₹4,921 cr (+55% YoY, inflated by JB Pharma consolidation), EBITDA ₹1,664 cr (margin 33.8%), but PAT only ₹566 cr (+3% YoY) - revenue and profit growth have diverged sharply, which is the real story, not the headline 55%. Management says the pre-merger base business grew ~17% organically and JB's segment contributed ₹1,201 cr. Q4 FY26 (Mar-2026) showed the same pattern: revenue +42% YoY but PAT -27% YoY due to merger-related exceptional costs - flagged here explicitly because the two don't move together. Pre-merger quarters (Q3/Q4 FY25) looked cleaner: revenue growth of 3-8% with PAT growth of 11-14% and stable ~32.5% EBITDA margins. Management flagged a semaglutide supply disruption affecting sales through August 2026 and said cost synergies from the JB Pharma deal already exceed the ₹100 cr target versus a ₹90 cr plan.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 11% from its 31 July 2026 peak of ₹5,122.8, but that is an ordinary pullback, not a crash - there is no demerger or spin-off in the supplied corporate-action data to adjust for (only three plain 2:1 stock splits, in 2006, 2013 and 2022, which are already reflected in the price series). Longer term, returns have been strong and consistent: +30% over 1 year versus -9.5% for Nifty and +7% for peer Sun Pharma; +144% over 3 years versus Nifty's +17% and peer's +59%; +211% over 5 years versus Nifty's +25% and peer's +121%. This is a stock that has comfortably beaten both the market and its closest large peer across every horizon shown.
analysis.valuation_read: On trailing numbers the stock looks expensive - P/E near 77x and P/B near 18.5x (Screener-sourced; not independently cross-checked against a second terminal, so treat as indicative). Why it looks this expensive matters more than the number itself: trailing PAT is held down by one-off merger integration and amortisation charges from the JB Pharma deal, so the P/E overstates how costly the business really is on a clean-earnings basis. Even allowing for that, a P/B near 18.5x still reflects the market paying up for a quality, consistently profitable pharma franchise and growth expectations from the merger - whether that premium is justified depends on synergies showing up in PAT growth in coming quarters, not just revenue growth.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is a mix of real organic expansion and one large acquisition. The pre-merger base business grew about 17% organically in the most recent quarter per management, which looks volume/mix-led rather than margin-led since EBITDA margin has stayed in a fairly narrow 32-34% band for several quarters rather than expanding. The JB Pharma merger adds a step-change in scale (US generics, CDMO) but this is inorganic and should not be read as underlying business momentum.
analysis.health_read: EBITDA generation looks healthy and margins are stable, but profit is not yet keeping pace with revenue: PAT growth of just 3% YoY against 55% revenue growth, and an outright 27% PAT decline in the prior quarter, point to financial risk (debt and amortisation from the JB Pharma acquisition) rather than business risk. Total debt/equity has risen to roughly 1.14x after the acquisition, and ROCE (~15.2%) sitting well below ROE (~27.4%) suggests leverage is doing some of the work - something worth re-checking once post-merger balance sheet figures settle over the next couple of quarters.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter group (Torrent Investments) holds approximately 60.78%, with FIIs around 17.97% and DIIs around 12.87% as of the September 2026 quarter - but this breakdown came from aggregated sources, not a primary NSE/BSE shareholding filing, so treat it as indicative pending direct confirmation. No promoter pledging was found in the search, but this was also not independently verified against a primary filing - Not verified, check on Screener or the NSE shareholding disclosure. No marquee individual investor (of the kind sometimes seen on smaller-cap registers) appears on the shareholding list.
strengths: 1-year return of +30% against Nifty's -9.5% and peer Sun Pharma's +7%, with similar outperformance over 3 and 5 years
EBITDA margin has held steady in the 32-34% range across the last several quarters despite the merger
Both the Bileshwarpura and Dahej manufacturing plants cleared recent USFDA inspections with zero observations
Pre-merger organic base business grew ~17% in Q1 FY27 per management, and cost synergies from the JB Pharma deal already exceed the ₹100 cr target against a ₹90 cr plan
watchpoints: PAT has grown far slower than revenue for two straight quarters (+3% vs +55% in Q1 FY27; -27% vs +42% in Q4 FY26) due to merger-related costs - the gap needs to close for the growth story to hold
Debt/equity has risen to roughly 1.14x following the debt-funded JB Pharma acquisition, raising financial risk
An Executive Director, Amal Kelshikar, resigned effective 16 October 2026 - reason not detailed in available sources
Trailing P/E (~77x) and P/B (~18.5x) price in a lot of optimism about merger synergies; any slippage in integration could compress the multiple quickly
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results due 23 October 2026 - specifically whether PAT growth starts catching up to revenue growth, which would confirm the JB Pharma merger synergies are real rather than just adding scale with added debt costs.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly revenue/EBITDA/PAT figures and merger timeline cross-checked against Torrent's own press releases and multiple news outlets. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE, D/E) are from an aggregator (Screener-style source) and were not cross-verified against a second independent terminal - treat as approximate. Promoter holding percentage and pledging status, and FII/DII splits, could not be confirmed against a primary NSE/BSE shareholding filing and should be verified before publishing. No evidence found of a 'JG Chemicals' deal or a CuraTeQ CDMO tie-up referenced in some queries - these appear to not exist or to be confused with the JB Chemicals merger.
